systems where the agents are implemented via feed-forward ReLU neural networks and the environment is non-deterministic. These challenges become even more difficult in multi-agent settings, where failures can spread across interacting agents and become hard to diagnose. This thesis addresses these problems by developing interpretable methods for safety assurance in both single-agent and multi-agent RL. For single-agent RL, this thesis introduces a framework that combines local task and risk critics with a global abstract policy graph. Together, these components explain how an agent balances performance and safety, reveal adversarial vulnerabilities, support formal verification and risk-guided falsification, and enable runtime shielding without retraining. For multi-agent RL, this thesis develops gradient-based coupling analysis and a two-stage failure-forensics framework that identifies the true source of failure, distinguishes root causes from downstream effects, and traces failure propagation through interpretable contagion graphs. The proposed methods are evaluated on MuJoCo navigation tasks, a Type 1 diabetes dosing environment, Multi-Agent Particle Environments, and StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge benchmarks. The results show that these frameworks are able to explain policy behavior, uncover more safety violations than baseline verification and falsification methods, reduce unsafe behavior through shielding, and accurately identify root failure sources in multi-agent systems.
